turns.t: Morning, Joan, morning, Helen. Dreadful weather. Did you manage to park alright, or is the car park a disaster again?
Mum insisted on being right by the door, so I circled for twenty minutes. Anyway, we're here for the check-up after she was so poorly last month.
I like to be close to the door, dear. It's the rain.
Quite sensible. So, Joan, how have you been in yourself since then?
Oh, much better, thank you. Just ticking along, really.
Good. Let's talk about your chest. Have you been coughing at all?
No, I'm not coughing. Not that I've noticed.
Mum, you are. You're coughing at night. I can hear you through the wall.
Am I? I don't notice it, dear. I sleep like a log.
Okay, I'll keep both views in mind. Helen, how often do you hear it?
Most nights, a dry little cough. It doesn't go on for long, but it's there.
Thank you. Joan, what about the stairs, do you get puffed out?
No, I don't get puffed out. I do the stairs two at a time. Well, one at a time.
Lovely. Now, which pills are you taking at the moment?
Just the blood pressure one, and a stomach one. Helen has the list.
Amlodipine, 5 mg, once a day. And omeprazole, 20 mg, in the mornings.
Thanks. And the amlodipine is for your high blood pressure, is that right?
Yes, that's what I've got. High blood pressure, for years now.
Have you had any operations, Joan, at any time?
A hip replacement, about five years ago. Best thing I ever did.
Excellent. And have you ever smoked?
I gave up smoking twenty years ago. Forty a day... no, twenty a day. Ha.
Good for you. Let me check your numbers now. Pop your sleeve up for me.
Blood pressure 134 over 76, pulse 82, temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius, breathing 16 breaths per minute, and oxygen 96 percent.
Is that good?
Those are all pleasing. Now I'll listen to your chest, so take some nice deep breaths in and out.
Your chest sounds clear on both sides. You can relax now.
That's a relief to hear.
Let me explain my thinking. After being as poorly as you were, we like to look at the lungs again, to make sure everything has cleared.
Your numbers and the way your chest sounds suggest the lungs are healing as expected.
So do I need anything more?
I'd like to arrange a chest X-ray, just to be certain. It's the only way to see the lungs properly.
Does she have to book it herself?
No, my team will send the request today, and radiology will ring you with a time.
If the X-ray still shows a shadow, I'll see you again and we'll decide together what comes next.
And what if it's all clear?
Then you carry on as you are, and there's no need to come back about this.
And Mum's cough at night? Should we do something about that?
Let's see what the X-ray shows first. Helen, jot down which nights you hear it, so we have something concrete.
I will. Thanks, doctor.
Thank you, dear. Is it still raining?
Hard as ever. Take an umbrella, and mind the kerb on the way out.
